data.one_liner: A singleton-based config manager that loads JSON from assets, files, URLs or maps and exposes values via getters.
data.what_it_does: It merges configuration files into a single map and makes them available throughout a Flutter app. You can load from assets, file paths, URLs, or Dart maps, and override values at runtime.
use_when: You need a simple, non-reactive configuration store for small to medium apps.
You want to load configuration from multiple sources (assets, files, URLs) without extra dependencies.
You prefer a straightforward API over complex state management solutions.
avoid_when: You require reactive updates to UI when configuration changes.
You need strong type safety or compile-time validation of config keys.
You are building a large-scale app that already uses a dedicated state management library.
strengths: Easy to set up and use with minimal boilerplate.
Supports multiple loading sources (assets, path, URL, map).
Provides updateValue and clear methods for runtime overrides.
MIT license and small dependency footprint.
weaknesses: No reactive or stream-based updates – UI must be rebuilt manually.
Limited error handling documentation for load failures.
data.setup_notes: Add dependency in pubspec and call GlobalConfiguration().loadFromAsset or other load method before runApp.

alternatives.name: http
alternatives.why_pick_it: Use http for custom network fetching and manual parsing if you need more control over requests.
